title: He Pedalled a Plane 22 Miles Across the English Channel

scenes.text: In 1979, a man flew across the English Channel by pedalling.
scenes.keywords: pedal powered aircraft flying over sea

scenes.text: The plane was the Gossamer Albatross. Its wingspan was nearly 94 feet, and it weighed just 70 pounds. Less than the pilot.
Bryan Allen pedalled a bicycle drive that spun the propeller. No engine. Just his legs.
He flew about five feet above the waves for 22 miles.
It took two hours and 49 minutes of non-stop pedalling.
A plane lighter than its pilot, powered by one man.

description:
On 12 June 1979, Bryan Allen pedalled the Gossamer Albatross across the English Channel in 2 hours 49 minutes.
The human powered aircraft had a wingspan of nearly 94 feet and weighed about 70 pounds, less than its pilot. He flew roughly five feet above the water for about 22 miles, powered by muscle alone.
Could you pedal for nearly three hours? Tell us below.
first_comment: The whole plane weighed less than the man pedalling it. Would you dare to sit in it?
